# Open Source Notices

This app includes dictionary resources generated from SudachiDict source data.

- SudachiDict project: https://github.com/WorksApplications/SudachiDict
- The current workflow in this repository uses SudachiDict core and small source CSV files.

SudachiDict is provided under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
The bundled dictionary databases are modified, derived works: the
SudachiDict source CSVs are converted, filtered, merged with additional
vocabulary, and re-indexed into this app's own database format. They are
not the original SudachiDict distribution.
The upstream SudachiDict project also provides additional legal notices in its LEGAL document.
According to upstream documentation, SudachiDict includes UniDic and a part of NEologd.

See bundled documents for complete terms and notices:
- SudachiDict Apache License 2.0
- SudachiDict LEGAL

## Latin word suggestion lexicons

This app includes word frequency lists for Latin-script suggestions
(English / French / German / Italian), derived from:

- wordfreq (English, German, Italian word frequencies) — Robyn Speer et al.
  https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq — Data licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.
  wordfreq combines multiple corpora; per its terms we credit the authors
  of SUBTLEX (Marc Brysbaert et al.), OpenSubtitles/OPUS, Wikipedia,
  Google Books Ngrams, and the other sources listed in the wordfreq
  documentation. SUBTLEX is freely available data.
- Tatoeba (German sentences; used only to restore German capitalization
  and ß spellings) — https://tatoeba.org/ — Licensed under CC BY 2.0 FR.
- Wiktionary (German entry titles; fallback for German display forms) —
  https://de.wiktionary.org/ — Licensed under CC BY-SA.
- Lexique 3.83 (French) — B. New, C. Pallier.
  http://www.lexique.org/ — Licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

The bundled lists are cleaned, frequency-ranked subsets (about 15000
words for English/French/Italian and 60000 for German) generated by
tools/build_latin_suggestion_lexicon.py. As several of the above
sources are ShareAlike-licensed, the bundled word lists themselves
(LatinSuggestionLexicon_{en,fr,de,it}.txt) are provided under
CC BY-SA 4.0.

This app includes a kanji index for the radical-based single-character
picker, derived from:

- Unihan Database (Unicode Character Database) —
  https://www.unicode.org/charts/unihan.html
  Copyright (c) 1991-2025 Unicode, Inc. Distributed under the
  Unicode License (see https://www.unicode.org/license.txt).

The bundled index (KanjiRadicalIndex.txt) lists CJK Unified Ideographs
U+4E00-9FFF with their Kangxi radical and residual stroke count
(kRSUnicode), JIS X 0208 ku-ten code (kJis0), and Japanese readings
(kJapanese), generated by tools/build_kanji_radical_index.py.

## Word language model (Japanese Wikipedia)

This app includes a word n-gram language model (unigram/bigram cost
tables) whose statistics are derived from the text of Japanese
Wikipedia (https://ja.wikipedia.org/).

- Wikipedia text is available under the Creative Commons
  Attribution-ShareAlike License (CC BY-SA 4.0,
  https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) and the GNU Free
  Documentation License.
- The bundled tables contain aggregated word frequency statistics
  computed from Wikipedia dump data; no article text is included.
- We consider these aggregated statistics to be factual data rather
  than an adaptation of the articles. To the extent they are
  nevertheless considered an adaptation, the bundled tables are
  likewise provided under CC BY-SA 4.0.

## Emoji readings (Unicode CLDR)

This app includes Japanese readings for emoji candidates, derived from
the Unicode Common Locale Data Repository (CLDR) Japanese emoji
annotations (https://cldr.unicode.org/).

- Copyright (c) Unicode, Inc. Distributed under the Unicode License
  (https://www.unicode.org/license.txt).
- The bundled data (EmojiReadingVocab.json, generated from
  references/emoji.plist) is a cleaned and reading-normalized subset.
